results.evidence: Order Form Section 8: "This Order Form and any dispute arising out of or relating to it are governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to its conflict-of-laws principles. Any action arising out of or relating to this Order Form must be brought exclusively in the state or federal courts located in New York County, New York." Compare MSA 14.1–14.2 (Delaware law; exclusive Wilmington courts) and MSA 1.3 ("Order Form, then Service Level Schedule, then Master Services Agreement").
results.reason: The Order Form picks New York law and an exclusive New York County forum. The MSA picks Delaware law and an exclusive Wilmington forum. MSA 1.3 ranks the Order Form above the MSA, so the New York clause controls disputes 'relating to' the Order Form. The Order Form sets the fees, term and exclusivity. The MSA and the Service Level Schedule still point to Delaware, and Order Form Section 9 says the MSA applies 'except as stated.' Because each Order Form is one contract made up of the Order Form, the Schedule and the MSA (MSA 1.2), a single dispute could arguably fall under both exclusive-forum clauses. For Seinon, the customer, that means uncertain governing law, competing forum claims and a risk of parallel litigation. Nothing in the folder reconciles the two clauses or records that the split was intended. The Order Form is unsigned and is presented as a draft for review, so the problem can still be fixed before execution.

results.evidence: Order Form Section 4: "During the term of this Order Form, Customer will use Provider as its exclusive provider of all fulfillment, warehousing and logistics services for all Seinon products in all sales channels worldwide, including direct-to-consumer e-commerce, wholesale distribution and retail-store replenishment. Customer will not engage, and will cause its Affiliates not to engage, any third party to provide those services during the term of this Order Form."
results.reason: MSA Section 2.4 limits Seinon's exclusivity to North American (US/Canada) direct-to-consumer e-commerce fulfillment. It expressly preserves Seinon's freedom to use third parties in other channels and territories. The Order Form expands the obligation to all fulfillment, warehousing and logistics in all channels worldwide, and binds Seinon's Affiliates as well. MSA Section 1.3 puts the Order Form first in the order of precedence, so the broader clause controls. Order Form Section 9 confirms that Order Form terms override the Agreement. Poseirt's actual services are limited to Storefront orders shipped in the US and Canada from Reno (Order Form 5.2(c)). Seinon would therefore be locked out of other providers for wholesale, retail and international logistics that Poseirt does not perform, for 60 months plus automatic renewals. Nothing in the folder cures or narrows this, and the Order Form is unsigned, so the clause can still be negotiated.

results.evidence: MSA Section 9.2: "Each Order Form will renew automatically at the end of its Initial Term, and at the end of each Renewal Term, for a successive renewal term equal in length to its Initial Term (each, a "Renewal Term"). An Order Form will not renew if either party delivers written notice of non-renewal to the other party no earlier than 100 days and no later than 90 days before the expiration of the then-current term." Order Form No. 1, Section 2: "The Initial Term of this Order Form is 60 months from the Order Form Effective Date. This Order Form renews in accordance with Section 9.2 of the Agreement."
results.reason: The problem is present and still actionable. Read with the Order Form's 60-month Initial Term starting April 1, 2026, Section 9.2 gives Seinon only a 10-day non-renewal window (about Dec 21–31, 2030). Missing it locks Seinon into a further five years at $48,500 per month plus fulfillment fees. Seinon would also stay bound by the exclusivity, which the Order Form broadens to all channels worldwide. Nothing in the folder cures this. The Order Form expressly incorporates Section 9.2, and the MSA has no termination for convenience. Termination is available only for cause, insolvency, extended force majeure or SLS Chronic Failure. The clause is mutual, but Provider gains from continued fees and exclusivity, so the harm falls on Seinon as Customer. The documents are unsigned and the window has not arrived, so Seinon can still negotiate a longer or no-earlier-than-free notice period, shorter renewal terms, or a convenience termination right.

results.evidence: Section 10.2: "Customer will defend Provider ... against any third-party claim arising out of or relating to the Products or the Customer Materials, regardless of whether caused in part by Provider handling, storage or shipment of the Products." Section 11.3: "The limitations in Sections 11.1 and 11.2 shall not apply to either party's indemnification obligations under Section 10."
results.reason: Seinon gives the Section 10.2 indemnity, and the problem falls on Seinon. That indemnity covers product liability, recall and customs claims even where Poseirt's own handling, storage or shipment contributed to the claim. Section 11.3 removes both the cap and the consequential-damages exclusion for all Section 10 indemnities. Poseirt's only indemnity (10.1) is a narrow Platform IP indemnity, so its uncapped exposure stays limited while Seinon's is broad and unlimited. Nothing in the Order Form or the Service Level Schedule narrows 10.2 or restores a cap. The Schedule's cap override in Section 6.3 concerns only Provider's Security Incident liability and works against Seinon, not in its favor. All signature blocks are blank, so the terms are still open to negotiation and the issue remains actionable.

results.evidence: Schedule Section 6.3: "Service Credits and Customer's termination right under Section 6.2 are Customer's sole and exclusive remedies for any Service Failure, including any Security Incident. Notwithstanding Section 11.3 of the MSA, Provider's aggregate liability arising out of or relating to Security Incidents shall not exceed the cap set out in Section 11.2 of the MSA."
results.reason: The problem is present and hurts Seinon. MSA 11.3(b) removes Security Incidents, including Poseirt's Section 8.3 obligations, from the 12-month-fees cap. MSA 8.3(c) makes Poseirt reimburse Seinon's notification, credit monitoring and call-center costs. Schedule 6.3 overrides both protections in two ways. It makes service credits and Chronic Failure termination the exclusive remedy for a Security Incident, which is defined as a Service Failure in Schedule 2(e). The only credit for that is SL-10 at 5% of the Monthly Platform Fee, per incident, for late notice. It also expressly re-imposes the 11.2 cap notwithstanding 11.3. MSA 1.3 ranks the Service Level Schedule above the MSA, so the Schedule controls. Nothing in the Order Form or elsewhere in the folder cures or limits this. The Schedule is unsigned, so the point is still open to negotiation before execution and remains actionable.
